messages:
maria: Heads-up — eu-central1 janitor heartbeats drifted ~6m, scrub concurrency jumped ~220, nvme IOPS spiked and ~30 GPU attaches failed/queued. Prom graphs show scrub_rate and attach_waits climbing.
ashok: Can you paste the PromQL or a link to the graph?
maria: promQL snippet: `sum(rate(janitor_jobs_active[1m])) by (zone)` then filter zone=eu-central1 -> saw ~220. Also `sum(increase(gpu_attach_failures[5m]))` jumped to 28.
storage-bot: :warning: ALERT: janitor_concurrency > 200 in eu-central1 for 5m — incident INC-5123 created.
joel: Can we throttle janitor quickly? Either env var or scale the deployment down. Want to avoid prolonged attach queue.
tara: Careful — throttling will grow scrub backlog. More backlog -> higher risk of latent badblocks and longer repair windows. Tradeoff between immediate attach availability and long-term wear/corruption risk.
nashok: Proposal: immediate canary throttle for eu-central1-c with env `JANITOR_MAX_CONCURRENCY=40`.
nashok: Command I plan to run: `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/janitor JANITOR_MAX_CONCURRENCY=40 --record --context=eu-central1-c`
nashok: Rollback (if bad): `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/janitor JANITOR_MAX_CONCURRENCY=200 --record`
maria: SGTM. I'll kick the canary and monitor attach queue + nvme_iops per host. Canary scope: eu-central1-c only.
deploy-bot: rollout started for deploy/janitor (canary) in eu-central1-c by maria — revision v2026.03.23-canary
joel: Also toggle attach fallback for heavy callers: set `ROUTE_ATTACH_FALLBACK=dedicated` in our router to divert 25% of attaches to dedicated pool until stable.
joel: Quick command: `curl -XPOST https://ops.internal/flags -d '{"flag":"route_attach_fallback","value":"dedicated","percent":25}'`
tara: FYI cost hit: diverting 25% to dedicated estimated +$3k/day on current qps. Acceptable short-term to avoid product impact?
maria: OK to proceed. Will watch: attach_wait_time, gpu_attach_failures, nvme_write_iops, host_smart_errors. If stable for 15m we gradually lift throttle. Will post metrics.
nashok: I'll stay on pager for next 30m. If anything looks off I can roll back quickly.
maria: Thanks — pinging @oncall in #eng-oncall just in case. :thumbsup:
storage-bot: NOTE: INC-5123 updated: runbook step 2 executed (canary throttle). Monitor: nvme_iops per host, attach queue length.
maria: Update 10m: attach failures down to 3 in last 5m, nvme_iops back to baseline, canary looks good. Proceeding to roll throttle to eu-central1-a/b next.
joel: Thx. After full region throttle, let's schedule a controlled backlog drain window overnight to avoid backlog accumulation.
